article_content: Ukraine's drone fleet has been relentlessly striking Russian positions, achieving an 'absolute record' in the number of targets hit during the past week, according to a Ukrainian official. From October 30 to November 6, Ukrainian drones allegedly struck 335 Russian targets. These figures were presented by Ukraine's Minister of Digital Transformation, Mykhailo Fedorov, in a Telegram post. 'Last week, our troops hit 335 Russian strongholds: an absolute record,' Fedorov stated on X. Both platforms detailed the claimed victories. As with all Ukrainian reports on Russian casualties, these numbers remain unverified. Western officials occasionally provide different statistics, although Ukraine's claims about specific equipment destruction can often be validated. The unverified report indicated that during this record-breaking week, Ukraine also eliminated 36 tanks, 83 armored combat vehicles, 18 self-propelled artillery systems, and 72 trucks. Fedorov regularly shares updates on Ukrainian drone operations. Last week, he posted data asserting that between October 23 and October 30, Ukrainian drones targeted 65 howitzers, 42 tanks, and 14 self-propelled artillery units. Since the war began, Ukraine has extensively utilized drones to attack Russian forces, destroy expensive tanks, and damage naval vessels. However, military analysts have noted that Ukraine still lags behind Russia in drone technology. Melissa Haring, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, highlighted the shortage of skilled drone pilots and high-quality drones after a recent visit to Ukraine's front lines. 'They're substandard,' she remarked about the drones. 'Manufactured in Chinese factories, they lack precision and often arrive defective.' Ukraine aims to address this by reducing dependence on China and boosting domestic drone production, as mentioned by Fedorov in September. Meanwhile, Russia is reportedly using drones equipped with engines purchased from the Chinese e-commerce platform AliExpress and larger Iranian-made Shahed-136 drones. Additionally, Russian forces employ Lancet drones, which loiter near targets before striking, effectively disrupting Ukraine's counteroffensives.
translated_content: Ukrajinska flota dronova neumorno udara ruske pozicije, postigavši 'apsolutni rekord' u broju pogođenih meta tokom prošle sedmice, prema ukrajinskom zvaničniku. Od 30. oktobra do 6. novembra, ukrajinski dronovi su navodno pogodili 335 ruskih meta. Ove brojke je predstavio ukrajinski ministar digitalne transformacije, Mihajlo Fedorov, u objavi na Telegramu. 'Prošle sedmice, naše trupe su pogodile 335 ruskih uporišta: apsolutni rekord', rekao je Fedorov na X-u. Obje platforme su detaljno opisale navodne pobjede. Kao i sve ukrajinske izvještaje o ruskim žrtvama, ove brojke ostaju neprovjerene. Zapadni zvaničnici povremeno daju različite statistike, iako se ukrajinske tvrdnje o uništavanju specifične opreme često mogu potvrditi. Neprovjereni izvještaj je pokazao da je tokom ove rekordne sedmice Ukrajina također uništila 36 tenkova, 83 oklopna borbena vozila, 18 samohodnih artiljerijskih sistema i 72 kamiona. Fedorov redovno dijeli ažuriranja o ukrajinskim operacijama dronova. Prošle sedmice objavio je podatke tvrdeći da su između 23. i 30. oktobra ukrajinski dronovi napali 65 haubica, 42 tenka i 14 samohodnih artiljerijskih jedinica. Od početka rata, Ukrajina je intenzivno koristila dronove za napad na ruske snage, uništavanje skupih tenkova i oštećivanje brodova. Međutim, vojni analitičari su primijetili da Ukrajina i dalje zaostaje za Rusijom u tehnologiji dronova. Melissa Haring, viši saradnik Atlantskog vijeća, istakla je nedostatak kvalifikovanih pilota dronova i visokokvalitetnih dronova nakon nedavnog posjeta ukrajinskim frontovima. 'Oni su loše kvalitete', rekla je o dronovima. 'Proizvedeni u kineskim fabricama, nedostaje im preciznost i često stižu defektni.' Ukrajina nastoji riješiti ovaj problem smanjujući zavisnost od Kine i povećavajući domaću proizvodnju dronova, kao što je Fedorov spomenuo u septembru. U međuvremenu, Rusija navodno koristi dronove opremljene motorima kupljenim sa kineske e-trgovinske platforme AliExpress i veće iranske dronove Shahed-136. Pored toga, ruske snage koriste Lancet dronove, koji lebde u blizini meta prije udara, efikasno ometajući ukrajinske kontraofanzive.
